title: Deploy contract (deploy/deploy.json)
description: Per ADR-0103 D5. Lives in the DEPLOYED repo at deploy/deploy.json and is read FROM THE TAG BEING DEPLOYED, never from the working tree — a release that changes how it must be deployed carries that change in the same commit. The Runner-side runner is generic; everything system-specific is here.

^//.//: A documentation key. Ignored by the runner and permitted at every object in this schema, because the contract is read FROM THE TAG and therefore cannot be edited after release: a schema that forbids a comment key strands every already-tagged system that used one.

contract_version.description: Schema generation. The runner refuses a contract_version it does not know rather than guessing which fields it can ignore.

system.description: System id, kebab (ADR-0006 naming). MUST match the directory the runner deploys into; a mismatch is refused, because a contract that names another system is either a bad copy-paste or a repo being deployed as something it is not.

units.description: launchd LABELS this system owns — the <key>Label</key> value, NEVER the plist filename. The two differ in practice (one member's com.<member>.plist holds label com.<member>.<job>), and a runner that bootstraps a filename silently restarts nothing. An empty list is legitimate and means 'deploying this changes files, not processes' (a CLI, a library) — it is not the same as 'unknown'.

restart.description: What a deploy has to DO to the units for the new code to be the code that runs. `kickstart` restarts a loaded service now (`launchctl kickstart -k`) — correct for an always-on daemon. `reload` boots the unit out and back in, for a plist whose own contents changed. `none` is for a SCHEDULED one-shot: launchd re-execs the program at each fire, so the next fire already runs the new tag, and kickstarting it would instead fire the job at an arbitrary hour — which for a job whose timing is its point means running it at 3am. `none` is a real deployment strategy, not a way of skipping the step.

^//.//: A documentation key. Ignored by the runner and permitted at every object in this schema, because the contract is read FROM THE TAG and therefore cannot be edited after release: a schema that forbids a comment key strands every already-tagged system that used one.

deps.description: How to materialize the runtime environment in the deploy tree. Offline-safe and pinned wherever the tool supports it.

kind.description: none = the tag is runnable as checked out (stdlib only, or an env owned elsewhere).

args.description: Extra arguments appended to the sync command.

state.description: Repo-relative paths that are gitignored but must EXIST in the deploy tree for the system to run. A tag checkout never touches ignored files, so these survive every deploy and rollback once present; the runner's only job is to SEED them on the first deploy, by COPYING. It never moves and never overwrites an existing path (ADR-0103 D3). NOTE WHAT IS NOT HERE: the path to copy FROM. That is machine-shaped, and this file is tracked in the system's own repo — a Runner path committed here would be WI-0132's defect wearing a new hat. Seed sources live in the deploying machine's gitignored deploy/seed-paths.local.json.

oneOf.description: THE PRE-OBJECT FORM, still accepted: a bare string is the repo-relative path, equivalent to {"path": <string>, "required": false}. Kept because a contract is read from the tag and cannot be edited after release — an already-cut member release carries this form, and dropping it strands that release rather than correcting it (WI-0358). The runner normalises it to the object form at read time, so nothing downstream sees two shapes.

^//.//: A documentation key. Ignored by the runner and permitted at every object in this schema, because the contract is read FROM THE TAG and therefore cannot be edited after release: a schema that forbids a comment key strands every already-tagged system that used one.

path.description: Repo-relative path in the deploy tree.

required.description: true = the deploy fails before anything is restarted if this path is absent after seeding. Use for state the system cannot start without; leave false for caches.

^//.//: A documentation key. Ignored by the runner and permitted at every object in this schema, because the contract is read FROM THE TAG and therefore cannot be edited after release: a schema that forbids a comment key strands every already-tagged system that used one.

smoke.description: A fast check that must exit 0 BEFORE any unit is restarted. This is the gate that makes a bad tag a non-event: it runs against the new tree while the OLD version is still serving, so a failure costs nothing but a rollback of files nobody was reading yet.

^//.//: A documentation key. Ignored by the runner and permitted at every object in this schema, because the contract is read FROM THE TAG and therefore cannot be edited after release: a schema that forbids a comment key strands every already-tagged system that used one.

verify.description: Post-restart aliveness check — does the thing that is now running actually work? Failure here triggers the full rollback (previous tag, re-sync, restart, confirm the old version healthy) and a loud escalation, because unlike a smoke failure this one happened with production already switched.

settle_seconds.description: Wait after restart before verifying, for a unit that needs a moment to bind a port or write its first line.

^//.//: A documentation key. Ignored by the runner and permitted at every object in this schema, because the contract is read FROM THE TAG and therefore cannot be edited after release: a schema that forbids a comment key strands every already-tagged system that used one.

apply.description: Override for systems whose 'deploy' is not a launchd restart — a cloud-deployed system whose apply verb is its own deploy tooling, run from the machine that holds that system's deploy credentials (ADR-0103 D8 shape 2). When present, the runner runs this INSTEAD of the units restart; smoke and verify still bracket it.

rerunnable.description: WI-0411. true = this member declares that re-running `cmd` for a tag ALREADY on the tree is safe, so a sweep that finds no apply receipt for that tag may run it. Default false keeps the behaviour every already-tagged system has today: the tree holding the tag short-circuits the sweep and the apply is never re-run. It lives in the contract rather than the registry because idempotency is a property of the apply SCRIPT, which ships in the same tag as this declaration — so a member opts in when it next cuts, which is also the moment somebody has looked at the script.
